projects.title: Memory Leak Diagnostics with Custom malloc/free Wrappers
projects.description: Memory leaks occur when heap memory allocated via `malloc()` is never returned via `free()`. Implement custom wrapper functions `custom_malloc()` and `custom_free()` that track active allocation counters and print memory leak diagnostics upon program termination. In this project, you will build Memory Leak Diagnostics Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Memory Allocation Hooks, Custom `malloc`/`free` Wrappers & Memory Leak Prevention
projects.exampleText: Audit dynamic memory allocation leaks using custom wrappers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Memory Leak Diagnostics ---
Total Allocations: 1
Total Frees: 1
Memory Leak Status: NO LEAKS DETECTED
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Allocation Counter**: Increment `alloc_count` in `custom_malloc()` and `free_count` in `custom_free()`.
2. **Leak Audit**: Memory leak detected if `alloc_count != free_count`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `custom_malloc()`, `custom_free()`: Custom wrappers tracking allocation counters to diagnose memory leaks.

projects.title: Dangling Pointer & Use-After-Free Detection Lab
projects.description: A Dangling Pointer points to a memory address that has already been deallocated using `free()`. Dereferencing it causes undefined behavior or security crashes (Use-After-Free). Audit pointer safety: ALWAYS set `ptr = NULL` immediately after calling `free(ptr)`! In this project, you will build Dangling Pointer Detector in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dangling Pointer Mechanics, Use-After-Free Vulnerabilities & Safe NULL Pointer Resets
projects.exampleText: Detect use-after-free pointer vulnerabilities
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dangling Pointer & Use-After-Free Detection ---
Detected Use-After-Free: Pointer dereferenced after free() call; set pointer = NULL to fix.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dangling State**: Freeing `ptr` leaves pointer address intact pointing to invalid memory.
2. **Safe Reset**: Assign `ptr = NULL`; check `if (ptr != NULL)` before dereferencing.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dangling_pointer_demo()`: Solves Dangling Pointer & Use-After-Free Detection.

projects.title: Buffer Overflow & Out-of-Bounds Memory Audit
projects.description: Buffer Overflows occur when writing data past the allocated array boundaries (`arr[i]` for `i >= N`), corrupting adjacent stack or heap RAM variables. Build boundary assertion guards and audit buffer overflow vulnerabilities! In this project, you will build Buffer Overflow Audit Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Buffer Overflow Attacks, Stack/Heap Corruption & Array Boundary Assertions
projects.exampleText: Audit buffer overflow write violations past array boundary
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Buffer Overflow & Out-of-Bounds Memory Audit ---
Detected Out-of-Bounds Write at array index 10 (valid range 0..9).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Boundary Violation**: Array of size N valid for indices `0 .. N-1`.
2. **Index Guard**: Assert `0 <= idx < N` before reading/writing array memory.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `buffer_overflow_audit_demo()`: Solves Buffer Overflow & Out-of-Bounds Memory Audit.

projects.title: Double Free Exception Diagnostics
projects.description: Calling `free(ptr)` TWICE on the same pointer causes heap corruption, leading to process crashes (`SIGABRT`). Track freed pointer addresses in a diagnostic lookup table to detect and intercept Double Free exceptions gracefully! In this project, you will build Double Free Diagnostic Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Double Free Exceptions, Heap Allocator Metadata & Graceful Signal Interceptions
projects.exampleText: Intercept double free memory exceptions
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Double Free Exception Diagnostics ---
Caught Double Free Exception: Memory block at 0x7ffd8a92 already freed!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Double Free Crash**: Freeing memory block twice corrupts glibc heap allocator bins.
2. **Diagnostic Table**: Track freed addresses; throw diagnostic error if address freed twice.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `double_free_diagnostics_demo()`: Solves Double Free Exception Diagnostics.

projects.title: Memory Alignment & Struct Padding Visualizer
projects.description: CPUs require 32-bit (4-byte) or 64-bit (8-byte) word alignment in RAM. Compilers insert invisible **padding bytes** inside C structs to align data fields, increasing total `sizeof(struct)`. Visualize struct layout offsets using `offsetof()`! In this project, you will build Struct Padding Visualizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: CPU Memory Alignment, Struct Padding Bytes, `offsetof()` Macro & Memory Reordering
projects.exampleText: Visualize struct padding bytes and alignment offsets
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Memory Alignment & Struct Padding Visualizer ---
Unpadded Struct Size: 12 bytes (3 bytes padding added by compiler for 4-byte CPU alignment).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Alignment Rule**: 4-byte `int` field must start at RAM address divisible by 4.
2. **Field Reordering**: Reorder struct fields from largest to smallest to minimize padding.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `struct_padding_demo()`: Solves Memory Alignment & Struct Padding Visualizer.

projects.title: Pointer Arithmetic vs Array Indexing Tracing
projects.description: In C, `*(ptr + i)` is strictly equivalent to `arr[i]`. Adding `1` to a pointer `ptr` advances the address in RAM by `sizeof(*ptr)` bytes (e.g. 4 bytes for `int*`). Trace pointer increment operations and memory addresses in C! In this project, you will build Pointer Arithmetic Tracer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Pointer Arithmetic Mechanics, Type Scale Multipliers (`sizeof(T)`) & Array Subscript Equivalences
projects.exampleText: Trace pointer arithmetic address offsets
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Pointer Arithmetic vs Array Indexing Tracing ---
*(ptr + 2) == arr[2] (Offset by 2 * sizeof(int) = 8 bytes in RAM).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Scale Multiplier**: `ptr + i` evaluates to address `(uintptr_t)ptr + i * sizeof(*ptr)`.
2. **Dereference Equivalence**: `*(ptr + i) == arr[i]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `pointer_arithmetic_demo()`: Solves Pointer Arithmetic vs Array Indexing Tracing.

projects.title: Stack Overflow via Unbounded Recursion Diagnostics
projects.description: Each recursive function call pushes a stack frame (local variables, return address, parameters) onto the call stack (typically 8 MB max limit). Unbounded recursion causes STACK OVERFLOW (`SIGSEGV`). Monitor call stack depth limits! In this project, you will build Stack Overflow Diagnostic Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Call Stack Frame Allocations, Stack Overflow Limits & Recursive Depth Guards
projects.exampleText: Diagnose stack overflow caused by unbounded recursion depth
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Stack Overflow via Unbounded Recursion Diagnostics ---
Stack Frame Exhaustion: Recursion depth exceeded maximum stack limit 8 MB!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Stack Frame Growth**: Every recursive invocation consumes stack memory for parameters and local variables.
2. **Depth Guard**: Track recursion depth `depth`; return error if `depth > MAX_SAFE_DEPTH`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stack_overflow_demo()`: Solves Stack Overflow via Unbounded Recursion Diagnostics.

projects.title: Dynamic Array Reallocation (Realloc) Memory Relocation Tracing
projects.description: `realloc(ptr, new_size)` resizes a heap buffer. If adjacent RAM space is unavailable, `realloc` allocates a NEW block elsewhere in RAM, copies old contents, frees old block, and returns new pointer! Trace address relocation events! In this project, you will build Realloc Tracing Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: `realloc()` Behavior, Heap Memory Relocation & Safe Pointer Reassignment
projects.exampleText: Trace memory block relocation during realloc expansion
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic Array Reallocation (Realloc) Tracing ---
Realloc expanded buffer capacity from 5 to 10 items (Relocated block to 0x7f88b0).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Relocation Event**: Compare original `ptr` address with returned `new_ptr` address.
2. **Safe Assignment**: `tmp = realloc(ptr, new_size); if (tmp) ptr = tmp;` prevents memory leaks.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `realloc_tracing_demo()`: Solves Dynamic Array Reallocation (Realloc) Tracing.

projects.title: Wild Uninitialized Pointer Auditing
projects.description: A Wild Pointer is a pointer that has not been initialized to any valid RAM address or `NULL`. Dereferencing or writing to a wild pointer corrupts arbitrary memory locations! ALWAYS initialize pointers to `NULL` (`int *p = NULL;`). In this project, you will build Wild Pointer Audit Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Wild Uninitialized Pointers, Garbage Address Prevention & NULL Pointer Initialization
projects.exampleText: Audit uninitialized wild pointers in C programs
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Wild Uninitialized Pointer Auditing ---
Caught Wild Pointer: Uninitialized pointer `ptr` contains garbage RAM address!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Uninitialized Trash**: Local pointers contain random stack garbage values upon creation.
2. **NULL Guard**: Initialize all pointers `int *p = NULL` at point of declaration.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `uninitialized_pointer_demo()`: Solves Wild Uninitialized Pointer Auditing.

projects.title: Pass-by-Value vs Pass-by-Reference (Pointer) Output Tracing
projects.description: Trace call stack differences between Pass-by-Value (creates local stack copy of variable; original unchanged) vs Pass-by-Reference via Pointers (`void func(int *p)` passing address; mutates original variable in caller stack frame). In this project, you will build Pass-by-Value vs Pass-by-Reference Tracer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Call Stack Parameter Passing, Pass-by-Value Copies & Pass-by-Pointer Reassignment
projects.exampleText: Trace variable mutation differences between Pass-by-Value and Pass-by-Reference
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Pass-by-Value vs Pass-by-Reference Tracing ---
Pass-by-Value: Original unchanged (x=10)
Pass-by-Reference (Pointer): Original mutated (x=20)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Pass-by-Value**: Function receives copy of value on stack frame; caller variable untouched.
2. **Pass-by-Pointer**: Function dereferences caller address `*p = val`; mutates caller variable.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `pass_by_ref_demo()`: Solves Pass-by-Value vs Pass-by-Reference Tracing.

projects.title: Valgrind Memcheck Log Parser & Automated Memory Diagnostic Tool
projects.description: Build an automated C log parser that reads Valgrind Memcheck output reports, extracts memory leak counts, invalid read/write locations, and uninitialized variable warnings, and outputs a clean diagnostic summary report! In this project, you will build Valgrind Log Parser in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Valgrind Memcheck Diagnostics, Automated Memory Log Parsing & Production Debugging
projects.exampleText: Parse Valgrind Memcheck report logs to summarize memory leaks
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Valgrind Memcheck Log Parser & Automated Diagnostic Tool ---
Parsed Valgrind Log: 1 leak found (40 bytes lost in 1 block at main.c:15).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Log Extraction**: Regex match 'definitely lost' and 'invalid read' lines in Valgrind output.
2. **Diagnostic Report**: Generate structured error report highlighting source code line numbers.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `valgrind_parser_demo()`: Solves Valgrind Memcheck Log Parser & Automated Diagnostic Tool.

projects.title: AddressSanitizer (ASan) Buffer Overflow Signal Interceptor
projects.description: AddressSanitizer (ASan) instrumented binaries detect out-of-bounds heap/stack reads and use-after-free at runtime. Implement custom signal handlers to intercept ASan crash signals (`SIGSEGV`/`SIGABRT`) and print stack backtraces! In this project, you will build ASan Signal Interceptor in C.
projects.learningOutcome: AddressSanitizer (ASan) Instrumentation, Signal Handling & Stack Backtrace Captures
projects.exampleText: Intercept AddressSanitizer buffer overflow crash signals
projects.exampleOutput:
--- AddressSanitizer (ASan) Buffer Overflow Interceptor ---
ASan Intercepted: global-buffer-overflow on address 0x00010c20.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **ASan Shadow Memory**: ASan checks 1-byte shadow memory for every 8-byte application memory.
2. **Signal Trap**: Trap invalid memory access signals to output backtraces.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `asan_interceptor_demo()`: Solves AddressSanitizer Buffer Overflow Interceptor.

projects.title: Custom Memory Arena / Bump Allocator Engine with Free List
projects.description: Standard `malloc()` calls overhead per allocation. A **Memory Arena / Bump Allocator** pre-allocates a large contiguous RAM block (e.g. 1 MB) and allocates objects by bumping a pointer forward in ultra-fast `O(1)` time! Reset entire arena in 1 operation. In this project, you will build Custom Memory Arena in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory Arena Allocators, Bump Pointer Allocation, O(1) Memory Speeds & Free Lists
projects.exampleText: Bump-allocate 1,000 nodes in 1 MB memory arena in O(1) time
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Custom Memory Arena / Bump Allocator Engine ---
Allocated 1 MB arena; bump-allocated 1,000 nodes in O(1) time without malloc overhead.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Arena Buffer**: Allocate 1 MB memory buffer `char arena[1024*1024]`.
2. **Bump Pointer**: `void* ptr = arena_head; arena_head += size;` allocates memory instantly.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `memory_arena_demo()`: Solves Custom Memory Arena / Bump Allocator Engine.

projects.title: Memory Fragmentation Audit Tool (External vs Internal Fragmentation)
projects.description: Audit heap memory fragmentation: 1) **Internal Fragmentation** (wasted space inside allocated blocks due to size alignment rounding); 2) **External Fragmentation** (total free RAM is sufficient, but fragmented into small non-contiguous blocks). Calculate fragmentation percentages! In this project, you will build Memory Fragmentation Audit Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Heap Memory Fragmentation Audits, Internal vs External Wasted RAM & Allocator Efficiency
projects.exampleText: Calculate external and internal heap memory fragmentation percentages
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Memory Fragmentation Audit Tool ---
External Fragmentation: 35% free heap space unavailable for contiguous 100 KB block.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Internal Fragmentation**: `wasted_internal = allocated_block_size - requested_size`.
2. **External Fragmentation**: `frag_ext = 1.0 - (largest_free_block / total_free_memory)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `memory_fragmentation_demo()`: Solves Memory Fragmentation Audit Tool.

projects.title: Garbage Collection Mark-and-Sweep Simulator in C
projects.description: Simulate a Java/Lisp-style **Mark-and-Sweep Garbage Collector** in C! 1) **Mark Phase**: Traverse object references starting from root stack pointers; mark accessible objects `reachable = true`; 2) **Sweep Phase**: Iterate heap blocks; free unreachable objects (`reachable == false`)! In this project, you will build Mark-and-Sweep GC Simulator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Garbage Collection Architecture, Mark-and-Sweep Graph Traversals & Unreachable Object Sweeps
projects.exampleText: Simulate Mark-and-Sweep garbage collection sweep on heap objects
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Garbage Collection Mark-and-Sweep Simulator ---
GC Mark Phase: Identified 12 reachable objects from root stack.
GC Sweep Phase: Reclaimed 5 unreachable objects (200 bytes freed).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Mark Phase**: DFS from root stack pointers; set `marked = 1` on visited heap nodes.
2. **Sweep Phase**: Loop all allocated heap objects; if `marked == 0`, call `free()` and unlink.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `mark_and_sweep_gc_demo()`: Solves Garbage Collection Mark-and-Sweep Simulator.

projects.title: Reference Counting Smart Pointer System in C
projects.description: Build a C++ `std::shared_ptr` equivalent Reference Counting Smart Pointer system in C! Wrap dynamic objects in a header containing `ref_count`. Increment `ref_count++` on copy; decrement `ref_count--` on release. Automatically call `free()` when `ref_count == 0`! In this project, you will build Reference Counting Smart Pointer System in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Reference Counting Smart Pointers, Automatic Deallocation & Shared Ownership Models
projects.exampleText: Manage object lifetime via reference counting smart pointers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Reference Counting Smart Pointer System ---
Ref Count = 2; decremented to 0 → Memory block automatically deallocated!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Retain Operation**: Increment `ptr->ref_count++` when adding owner reference.
2. **Release Operation**: Decrement `ptr->ref_count--`; if `ref_count == 0`, execute `free(ptr)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `ref_count_smart_ptr_demo()`: Solves Reference Counting Smart Pointer System.

projects.title: Stack vs Heap Memory Allocation Profiler
projects.description: Benchmark execution speeds of Stack Allocation (adjusting Stack Pointer register `SP` in 0.001 ns) vs Heap Allocation (`malloc()` requesting memory from OS kernel via `brk()` / `mmap()` in 45 ns). Profile speed differences across 1,000,000 allocations! In this project, you will build Stack vs Heap Memory Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Stack Pointer Assembly (`SP`) vs OS Kernel Heap Calls (`brk`/`mmap`), Nanosecond Benchmarks
projects.exampleText: Benchmark execution speeds of Stack allocation vs Heap malloc()
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Stack vs Heap Memory Allocation Profiler ---
Stack Allocation: 0.002 ns (SP sub)
Heap Allocation: 45.200 ns (malloc / OS kernel call)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Stack Allocation**: Subtracts bytes directly from stack pointer register `RSP` in 1 clock cycle.
2. **Heap Allocation**: Searches heap bins, locks mutexes, and executes kernel calls.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stack_vs_heap_profiler_demo()`: Solves Stack vs Heap Memory Allocation Profiler.

projects.title: Deep Copy vs Shallow Copy Dynamic Memory Diagnostics
projects.description: Audit Shallow Copy bugs (copying struct pointers directly, causing both objects to share the same heap memory address and crash on Double Free!) vs Deep Copy (allocating new independent heap buffers and copying content bytes)! In this project, you will build Deep Copy vs Shallow Copy Diagnostic Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Deep Copy vs Shallow Copy Invariants, Pointer Aliasing Bug Fixes & Independent Memory Buffers
projects.exampleText: Audit shallow copy double-free bugs and implement deep copy fixes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Deep Copy vs Shallow Copy Dynamic Memory Diagnostics ---
Shallow Copy Bug: Both pointers point to same memory address 0x7f90a0 (Double Free Hazard).
Deep Copy Fixed: Allocated separate heap buffer for cloned object.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Shallow Copy Bug**: `dest.data = src.data;` duplicates pointer address; freeing both crashes.
2. **Deep Copy Fix**: `dest.data = malloc(size); memcpy(dest.data, src.data, size);`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `deep_vs_shallow_copy_demo()`: Solves Deep Copy vs Shallow Copy Dynamic Memory Diagnostics.

projects.title: Out-of-Memory (OOM) Graceful Error Recovery Engine
projects.description: Production software must handle `malloc()` returning `NULL` when system RAM is exhausted. Implement an OOM Error Recovery Engine that catches `NULL` returns, flushes non-essential cache buffers, triggers garbage compaction, and retries allocation safely! In this project, you will build OOM Recovery Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Out-of-Memory (OOM) Management, `malloc` NULL Handling & Graceful Cache Flushes
projects.exampleText: Handle malloc NULL returns gracefully via cache buffer flushing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Out-of-Memory (OOM) Graceful Error Recovery ---
Caught malloc NULL return value; flushed non-essential cache buffers and recovered safely.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **NULL Check**: `ptr = malloc(size); if (!ptr) trigger_oom_handler();`.
2. **Cache Eviction**: OOM handler frees low-priority cached objects to release RAM.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `oom_recovery_demo()`: Solves Out-of-Memory (OOM) Graceful Error Recovery Engine.

projects.title: Dynamic Array Boundary Guard Canary Bytes
projects.description: Protect heap buffers against buffer overflow corruption using **Canary Bytes**! Surround allocated memory buffers with magic sentinel bytes (e.g. `0xDEADBEEF`). Periodically verify canary values: if magic bytes are modified, a buffer overflow occurred! In this project, you will build Boundary Guard Canary Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Canary Byte Sentinels (`0xDEADBEEF`), Buffer Overflow Detection & Memory Protection
projects.exampleText: Surround dynamic memory buffers with magic canary bytes to detect overflows
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic Array Boundary Guard Canary Bytes ---
Canary Check Passed: Magic bytes 0xDEADBEEF intact at array boundaries.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Canary Placement**: Write `0xDEADBEEF` magic bytes before and after allocated buffer.
2. **Canary Audit**: Verify canary bytes before freeing; flag buffer overflow if modified.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `canary_bytes_guard_demo()`: Solves Dynamic Array Boundary Guard Canary Bytes.

projects.title: High-Performance Fixed-Size Slab Allocator Kernel
projects.description: Kernel memory allocators (e.g. Linux Slab Allocator) manage fixed-size object slabs (e.g. 32-byte nodes) using a singly linked free list stored directly inside free slab slots! Allocates and frees in lightning `O(1)` time with ZERO internal fragmentation. In this project, you will build Fixed-Size Slab Allocator Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Linux Kernel Slab Allocators, In-Slot Free Lists & Zero Fragmentation O(1) Allocations
projects.exampleText: Allocate 32-byte object slabs in O(1) time using Kernel Slab Allocator
projects.exampleOutput:
--- High-Performance Fixed-Size Slab Allocator Kernel ---
Allocated 32-byte object slabs in O(1) time with 0% fragmentation.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **In-Slot Pointer**: Unallocated 32-byte slab slot stores pointer to next free slab slot.
2. **O(1) Pop/Push**: Pop free list head on `slab_alloc()`; push to free list head on `slab_free()`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `slab_allocator_demo()`: Implements High-Performance Fixed-Size Slab Allocator Kernel.

projects.title: Hardware Performance Counters Cache Line Miss Profiler (Perf / PAPI)
projects.description: Profile hardware CPU L1/L3 cache line misses for data structure access patterns using OS performance counters (`perf_event_open`). Demonstrate why sequential array traversals have 99% cache hit ratios while pointer-chasing linked lists suffer heavy cache misses! In this project, you will build Cache Line Miss Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Hardware Performance Counters (`perf`), Cache Line Miss Profiling & Memory Access Locality
projects.exampleText: Profile CPU L1/L3 cache misses for sequential vs pointer-chasing loops
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Hardware Performance Counters Cache Line Miss Profiler ---
Profiled L1/L3 Cache Line Misses: Sequential Loop (12 misses) vs Random Loop (4,500 misses).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Perf Event Open**: Configure hardware CPU PMU counters for `PERF_COUNT_HW_CACHE_MISSES`.
2. **Locality Comparison**: Sequential memory prefetching eliminates cache misses.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cache_miss_profiler_demo()`: Solves Hardware Performance Counters Cache Line Miss Profiler.

projects.title: Lock-Free Thread-Safe Memory Pool Engine using Atomic CAS
projects.description: High-throughput multi-threaded servers allocate memory using a Lock-Free Memory Pool. Manages free list pointers using atomic Compare-And-Swap (`atomic_compare_exchange_weak()`) operations, eliminating thread lock contention overhead! In this project, you will build Lock-Free Memory Pool Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Lock-Free Memory Pools, Atomic CAS Operations (`atomic_compare_exchange`) & Multi-Core Speeds
projects.exampleText: Allocate and free 100,000 memory blocks across 8 threads lock-free using atomic CAS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Lock-Free Thread-Safe Memory Pool Engine using Atomic CAS ---
Allocated and freed 100,000 memory blocks across 8 threads using atomic CAS lock-free free lists.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Atomic Free List**: Head pointer updated atomically via `atomic_compare_exchange_weak()`.
2. **ABA Protection**: Incorporate hazard pointers or tagged pointers to prevent ABA race condition.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lockfree_memory_pool_demo()`: Solves Lock-Free Thread-Safe Memory Pool Engine using Atomic CAS.

projects.title: Memory-Mapped Virtual Address Translation & Page Fault Diagnostic Engine
projects.description: Simulate Virtual Memory MMU address translation: translate Virtual Addresses `(Page Number, Offset)` to Physical RAM Frames using Page Tables! Intercept Page Fault exceptions (`SIGSEGV`) when accessing unmapped virtual pages in `mmap()` space! In this project, you will build Virtual Memory Translation Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: MMU Virtual Address Translation, Page Tables, Page Fault Exception Handling & `mmap` Space
projects.exampleText: Translate virtual address to physical RAM frame and handle page fault signals
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Memory-Mapped Virtual Address Translation & Page Fault Diagnostic Engine ---
Translated Virtual Address 0x7ffd8a92 to Physical RAM Frame 0x004a20 (Page Fault Handler Executed).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Page Table Lookup**: `page = vaddr >> 12`, `offset = vaddr & 0xFFF`.
2. **Page Fault Trap**: Catch unmapped page access; allocate physical frame and update page table.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `virtual_address_translation_demo()`: Solves Virtual Address Translation Diagnostic Engine.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory Telemetry & Leak Monitoring Kernel
